#1348. Fleetwood v Everton Cup Quarter-Final Ticket News

Everton can confirm ticketing arrangements for the Club’s Carabao Cup quarter-final against Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium on Thursday 17 December (8pm GMT kick-off).

The Club has received an allocation of 718 tickets, including six pairs of wheelchair spaces, for the eagerly-anticipated cup tie.

Following Fleetwood Town’s recent sell-out fixture against Arsenal, the League Two club has reviewed its stadium safety arrangements to accommodate operational requirements and maximise ticket availability for home supporters. These adjustments have resulted in a slightly reduced away allocation compared to the previous round but still accounts for just under 15 per cent of Highbury’s capacity.

With the allocation significantly smaller than those received for most Everton Premier League away fixtures, and demand expected to considerably exceed availability, tickets will be distributed through a ballot process.

The Club has previously consulted its fan groups on the fairest approach to allocating tickets for fixtures where demand exceeds availability, including occasions when the number of eligible supporters with maximum away credits is greater than the number of tickets available.

The Club has extended the away credits qualifying period to recognise supporters’ attendance over a longer period, reviewing ticketing data dating back to the 2021/22 season. However, even with an extended period of accumulated away credits, the number of eligible supporters still exceeds the available allocation. For this reason, a ballot process is therefore required.

The ballot will be open to 2026/27 Season Ticket Members who have accumulated 126 away credits across the 2021/22 to 2026/27 seasons, up to and including the Club’s recent away Premier League fixture against Newcastle United.

Supporters can check their qualifying away credit history by clicking here.

Further information on the fixtures included within the qualifying period can be found here.

Official Supporters’ Clubs will also be required to submit applications through the ballot process, with eligible members included in the same ballot as other qualifying supporters. Supporters’ Club members will only be eligible if they meet the required credit criteria.

The Club’s allocation includes seating in the Parkside Stand and standing tickets in the Percy Ronson Stand.

The Supporter Number of every eligible entrant must be provided when submitting a ballot application.

The ballot application window will open at 10am on Thursday 19 November, closing at 4pm on the same day.

Box Office opening times can be found HERE.

Supporters may apply individually or as part of a group of up to six family and friends, provided every member of the group meets the qualifying criteria.

Each supporter or Membership number can only be entered into the ballot once. Supporters included within a group application cannot submit a separate individual application or be included in another group.

All applicants will be notified of the outcome of their ballot application by 4pm on Friday 20 November.

In recognition of the exceptionally limited allocation, and to ensure supporters are not disadvantaged in future away ticket applications, all successful and unsuccessful ballot applicants will still receive an away credit for the fixture. This will be applied to their account once the match has been played.

The Club has received six pairs of wheelchair spaces, which are included within the overall allocation of 718 tickets.

Supporters who require wheelchair accommodation must submit their applications in writing directly to Everton’s Accessibility Team during the Ballot opening timeline (Thursday 19 November between 10am and 4pm). Tickets will be issued to supporters who meet the qualifying criteria based on previous away credit history.

Coach travel costs £35 and will depart from Goodison Park at 4:30pm. Supporters must be Travel Club members to purchase coach tickets. The Travel Club Membership costs just £5.

Everton has also been able to secure a limited number of hospitality packages for this fixture, offering supporters an alternative way to experience the quarter-final at Highbury.

Supporters interested in securing a hospitality package can register their interest by CLICKING HERE.

Supporters are reminded that it is an offence under Section 166 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 for any unauthorised person to resell football tickets.

Further information on the Club’s position regarding ticket touting can be found here.

Watch the quarter-final at Hill Dickinson Stadium

For Evertonians unable to attend the fixture at Highbury Stadium, the Club will host a special live screening of the quarter-final at Kendall’s Social at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Supporters will have the opportunity to come together with fellow Blues at the Club’s waterfront home to watch the action and get behind the team as Everton look to secure a place in the Carabao Cup semi-finals.

For more information on the screening and how to attend, please CLICK HERE.

#1347. Why Man United staff feel treatment of Michael Carrick was 'disgusting' and the comment from Omar Berrada that raised eyebrows as club legend is put out of his misery - and Mauricio Pochettino gets set to take over

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 14:25 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:15 EST, 13 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino would have been fast asleep in his hotel room in the quirky American town of Trilith when Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sat down with Michael Carrick at Carrington Thursday morning and confirmed the worst-kept secret in football.

It was time for Carrick to vacate the head coach’s office at Manchester United, and safe to say Pochettino will have his feet under the desk this time next week.

Carrick arrived at 7.50am but, unlike the last two days, he was no longer wearing his United training gear.

The agonising wait to be put out of his misery was over, and the club’s chief executive and director of football duly administered the last rites before Carrick left at 10.18am.

The decision was communicated to staff and Under-21s boss Adam Lawrence took training with the players who have remained at Carrington during the international break.

The first reports of Carrick’s sacking broke at 9.30am, but United insisted that they were premature and it wasn’t until 10.37am that the news was confirmed in a 142-word statement.

Michael Carrick finally left Carrington on Thursday morning after an agonising wait to be put out of his misery

Staff at Manchester United believe that the former club captain's treatment at the hands of their Ineos paymasters has been 'disgusting'

It's understood that his backroom staff - assistant Steve Holland, coaches Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, and goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson - have also gone. When Evans left on Wednesday night with his car piled high with cardboard boxes, it didn't bode well.

The treatment of Carrick and Evans, in particular, has upset staff. Two highly-respected figures at United, whose association with the club goes back more than 20 years, have been left hanging while their employers stumble over a succession plan.

Members of staff share Gary Neville’s view that Berrada and Wilcox meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, and making a move for Pochettino while Carrick had to keep driving past the cameras on his way into Carrington for the last three days, was ‘disgusting’.

It has also reignited anger over the 450 job cuts carried out by Ratcliffe and Ineos over the past three years while pouring millions down the drain in compensation.

The £10million to buy Pochettino and his staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation, and the pay-off owing to Carrick and Co, will push the cost of hiring and firing coaches in the Ineos era close to £50m.

No wonder eyebrows were raised when Berrada spoke at Sir Alex Ferguson’s 40th anniversary dinner at Old Trafford on Friday night and talked about building a culture at the club.

The feeling is that changing United’s head coach won’t make a shred of difference if there isn’t significant change higher up the chain.

It has once again turned the spotlight on the relationship between Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, who from February can force him to sell his 28 per cent holding to a third party for less than the £25-per-share he paid in 2024 unless he can match the offer and buy the club himself.

However, United sources say they had little choice but to sack Carrick with the club in the relegation zone, having decided to give him a stay of execution at the end of last month.

Since then, the club had carried out a comprehensive review and come to the conclusion that a record of one win from 10 Premier League games was unacceptable.

The sources indicated that the United board shared the frustration and anger felt by fans over the situation, and believe that a change of head coach will bring about an improvement from a squad that is far better than results would suggest.

While United praised Carrick for his ‘highest degree of professionalism’, there was only silence from the players on social media.

Many of them are on international duty, including Bruno Fernandes whose criticism of Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat to Como proved so damaging.

Following the announcement of Carrick's dismissal none of his former players - including Bruno Fernandes - were quick to say their goodbyes publicly

Meanwhile, his would-be successor Mauricio Pochettino is set to face the media on Friday

Pochettino will inherit this squad of players once he has completed his duties as US national team coach with the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is due to speak at 2.15pm Friday ahead of the first leg in Miami on Saturday night when he will face questions over the United job for the first time.

Pochettino is expected to stay in charge for the second leg in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning before flying to Manchester to meet the players and prepare for the crunch clash with Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

The US have been staying in Trilith, near their new training headquarters in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta, where they were also based before the World Cup.

It’s a unique place designed for the film industry and built around the Trilith Studios which are the largest outside Hollywood. The ideal place for Pochettino to prepare for life at Old Trafford.

He has embraced the American lifestyle since he was appointed US coach in September 2024, a few months after leaving Chelsea, and will be sorry to leave.

Pochettino is said to have developed a love of bourbon whiskey, country music and Nashville, with Ella Langley’s Choosin’ Texas one of his favourite tunes.

He has admitted crying over Miracle, the movie about the US hockey team made up of college kids famously beating the Soviet Union to the gold medal at the 1980 Winter Olympics.

But the pull of Manchester United was always going to be too great, and very soon he will be swapping Trilith for Old Trafford.

#1346. George & Armstrong Start In England Under-21s Friendly

Harrison Armstrong and Tyrique George both played an hour of England Under-21s’ 1-0 defeat to Portugal at Ashton Gate Stadium.

The Young Lions went behind to an Afonso Moreira goal in the 28th minute and were unable to find a way past keeper João Carvalho from there.

This was Armstrong’s first start for the Under-21s after making his debut as a substitute against Ireland in the previous international window, while George was making his 10th appearance at this level.

Lee Carsley’s side had already secured qualification for next summer’s UEFA U21 Euro finals in October, and are using these friendlies in preparation for the tournament in Albania and Serbia.

Armstrong and George return to action in Bristol on Monday 16 November, taking on France (7.30pm kick-off).

#1345. Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two big chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an important moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite quickly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb

“The performance was really good,” said Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix

Iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu

Still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

Ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very quickly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

There will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

So wasteful from Brighton... They have a great chance to put the ball into the box with a free kick, but De Cuyper wastefully launches it out of play. With Gross also stood over it, you expected him take it. Liverpool then make a late change as Tsimikas replaces Kerkez for the final few minutes.

Gakpo drives forward and smashes a wild long-range shot wide. His end-product has been lacking today, but he’s undoubtedly caused Brighton problems with his dribbling, movement and directness.

A spell of Brighton pressure ends as Rutter can’t quite find Kostoulas with a low cross. The young striker stays down and replays show that Jacquet stood on his foot as the defender attempted a clearance. However, it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR. There wasn’t much in the challenge at all.

Kerkez scampers into Brighton’s box, reaching the byline, but he can’t dig out a cross as the chance disappears. Brighton will need to throw everything forward soon.

Now, that double change from Liverpool is here. Barcola and Isak depart to large applause, with Ngumoha and Koumas cheered on as they run onto the pitch.

As expected, Rutter is on. He replaces Ayari, who will think back to his missed chance and shot off the post in the first half.

Gakpo brilliantly turns Costinha, who pulls the winger back to deservedly pick up a booking. Both sides look to be readying changes, with Ngumoha, Koumas and Rutter poised to enter the action.

Brighton seem to have hit a wall in this second half. They’ve struggled to create chances since the break. Liverpool are working really hard defensively.

Once again, Liverpool break through Gakpo. This time, it comes from a Brighton corner, but Gakpo’s cross for Isak at the back post is read by Dunk.

In his first involvement since entering the action, Nyoni ends a slick Brighton move by taking the ball off De Cuyper’s toe in the penalty area with a much-needed clearance. He seems to be limping after he was caught by De Cuyper.

Wirtz’s game is over and he departs to be replaced by Nyoni in Liverpool’s first change.

After some treatment for Wirtz, Vuskovic eventually takes the free kick. It’s in such an inviting position, but the defender gets too power on his strike and whips it over the bar.

This game is still very much in the balance, even though Liverpool have a two goal advantage, and it speaks volumes about both teams’ commitment to attack. The questions the respective head coaches are asking of their players are relentless but the players are responding by being adventurous in how they attack and where they want to get on the ball. How Andoni Iraola and Fabian Hurzeler deploy their substitutes will be significant.

Liverpool are holding firm, with Brighton yet to create an opportunity in this second half. Ayari is apprehended by Wirtz to win a free kick on the edge of the area. Despite committing the foul, Wirtz has stayed down and is clutching his ankle.

Brighton make another change and it’s a straight swap in midfield as Yalcouye replaces Chema Andres, who hobbles off the pitch.

With Brighton requiring at least two goals to avoid defeat, they’ll need to push a lot of men forward, which will open up space for Liverpool to exploit on the break. If there is one, the next goal in this game is crucial.

Liverpool break through Gakpo, who sprints from inside his own half into the penalty. He tries to release Isak, but his pass is intercepted by Vuskovic as he’s swarmed by the Brighton defence. Gakpo waited too long and should have played the pass earlier.

Kerkez isn’t switched on and fails to deal with a long ball, allowing Gomez to race in behind. Van Dijk covers Kerkez and blocks Gomez’s pass, with Kostoulas sprinting up in support.

We are back under way for the second half. Hurzeler has made one half-time alteration, with Hinshelwood replacing Boscagli, who was booked just before the break. Meanwhile, Liverpool are unchanged as they look to protect their two-goal advantage.

Wirtz’s wickedly deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s neat finish from close range mean Liverpool are two goals in front against Brighton. The visitors have also looked dangerous going forward, with Ayari wasting a golden chance when the score was still goalless, before hitting the post in the 36th minute. As it stands, this result would move Liverpool into fourth and a point behind Brighton, who need a massive second-half performance.

Two goals to the good for @LFC 😮‍💨 A Pascal Gross own goal puts the Reds ahead, before Alexander Isak fires in the second 🔴 https://t.co/AglQOyUIoY

Brighton are desperate to find a goal before the break as Kostoulas’ fierce shot is batted away by Alisson, whose goal is living a charmed life. Boscagli then receives a yellow card for blocking Barcola’s off-the-ball run.

No getting away from the fact that Brighton simply haven’t got started and it’s a huge surprise. What chances they have had came from Liverpool’s own shortcomings and it is impossible to think they will be so off the pace in the second period. Fabian Hurzeler has remained composed, which is more than can be said for Oliver Boscagli, who looks like he is playing pass the parcel, so anxious is he to get rid of the ball - often with a mistake.

On the counter, Gomez tries to find Ayari with a pass, but Jacquet’s touch knocks the ball out of Liverpool’s box. There will be three minutes of added time to end this half.

Araujo forces a save as he sprints forward from his right-back position to receive a clipped pass from Mac Allister, before shooting from a tight angle to sting the palms of Verbruggen with a drilled effort.

Gakpo drives at Brighton’s defence and then nearly squeezes a low cross to the supporting Isak, but Dunk’s crucial intervention with his outstretched leg prevents a chance.

Off the post for Brighton. Ayari shoots from an incredibly long way out as Brighton dispossess Mac Allister and Jacquet, however his curling effort agonisingly bounces against the post and out, with Alisson well beaten.

Despite falling two goals behind in this first half, Brighton have recorded 83% possession over the previous five minutes.

There’s a small confrontation between Vuskovic and Gakpo, which is quickly checked and cleared by VAR. In the next passage of play, Kerkez tees up Gakpo, who bursts into the box and reaches the byline, but his cross is blocked by Dunk.

A smooth Brighton move ends with Jacquet making a crucial block to deny Kostoulas from close range. Liverpool eventually scramble it clear. That’s a reminder of the threat that Brighton can pose.

Brighton look stunned. Since Ayari missed that chance, they’ve been swarmed by Liverpool, whose forwards are in the mood for some goals today.

Two goals in quick succession propel Liverpool into a commanding lead. So much credit must go to Barcola. He closes down Boscagli, beats the defender to the loose ball with his blistering pace and then delivers a pinpoint cross towards Isak, who gets across his marker at the near post to direct a first-time finish into the far bottom corner.

Gakpo bursts in behind Brighton’s defence and outpaces Vuskovic. From a tight angle, the winger shoots, forcing Verbruggen into a decent save. Liverpool are looking very slick in forward areas.

Welcome to Anfield, where we have just had four seasons in 10 minutes: rain was overtaken by sunshine, all the while the wind has been blowing past itself, the kind that wouldn’t just turn an umbrella inside out but carry you off into the distance. Racing was abandoned at Aintree, which is just two miles away, early this morning but there have been no such worries at Anfield. The pitch is actually well sheltered from the elements, so hopefully it won’t impact on the game too much. These sides both want to play football and we can safely say (famous last words) that it won’t be 0-0 at 90 minutes.

Even by his prodigious standards, this has been a different week for Rio Ngumoha. After the coming-of-age performance against Villarreal, so followed the slew of attention on social media.

A clip of his best moments during the chaotic 4-3 dispatching of the Spaniards, posted on Uefa’s official X account, attracted 1.2 million views and was liked more than 24,000 times. Hot on the heels came another video, this time when he was 11, when he nutmegged a dumbfounded cameraman.

Ngumoha has always had feet that move as quickly as the hands of street artists who perform tricks with cups and balls: now you see it, now you don’t. We live in an age where talent is quickly amplified and this young England international has it in bundles.

You saw it in those exhilarating 74 minutes: Ngumoha had his most touches in a game this campaign (51), most touches in the opposition box (12) and attempted the most dribbles (10), as well as creating the most chances (three) and providing two assists.

It is the first time an 18-year-old has produced such figures in the Champions League since Opta’s European records began in 2008-09.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Liverpool and Brighton & Hove Albion at Anfield.

Liverpool are on a three-game winning run in all competitions, and came from two goals behind in their previous outing in the Champions League on Tuesday, earning an enthralling 4-3 victory over Villarreal. Last weekend, Andoni Iraola’s men also initially fell behind against Brentford in the Premier League, but netted two second-half goals through Daniel Munoz and Alexander Isak to win 2-1 as their opponents finished with nine men.

In his programme notes, Liverpool boss Iraola was excited about the prospect of a second game in a week at home. “As someone who believes every single opportunity we have to play a game at this stadium and in front of our supporters is a privilege, I also feel very passionately that this is a period that we should continue to embrace,” he said.

“It is also a spell in which we will carry on being tested because the quality of the opposition dictates that there is no chance of anything else. Villarreal pushed us all the way in midweek and everything about the way Brighton have played so far this season tells us that it would be foolish to expect anything but the same today.”

Brighton have emerged as one of the surprise packages of the Premier League season thanks to their blistering start. Fabian Hurzeler’s side sit third in the table, having scored a whopping 23 goals in their opening seven games, while conceding just five. On Thursday, Brighton were unexpectedly held to a 0-0 draw by Czech outfit Jablonec, ending a run of six straight victories in all competitions. Nevertheless, they’re unbeaten since their 4-3 league loss to Chelsea back on August 30.

Defender Ferdi Kadioglu believes his team’s energy and fitness has played a huge role in their eye-catching form. “If you want to play how we play, you have to be very fit,” he said. “We were already fit last season, but I think it’s more that now everyone really understands what we need to do to win matches. That’s really clear this season, and everyone is doing it. Everyone is really focused on their task and doing it very well so far.”

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news following shortly.

#1344. Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada1,2,3. Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ18O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive εHf(t) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta2, the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin4. Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8–16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740–820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

a, Geological map of the early Precambrian rocks in the North China Craton94, showing the distribution of Archaean and Palaeoproterozoic rocks. b, Geological map of the Qian’an-Lulong area (modified after refs. 95,96,97), showing the spatial distribution of the early Archaean Muchangkou–Shimen Complex, which includes the Muchangkou Complex in the Huangbaiyu area and the Shimen Complex in the Labashan area16. c, Geological map of the Shimen Complex16. The complex is composed of Eoarchaean to Mesoarchaean granitoids and supracrustal rocks as enclaves of varying sizes in undeformed 2.5-Gyr-old potassic granite.

a, View of the hill showing the outcrop location of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss. b, The 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss is aligned parallel to the foliation in the 3.5-Gyr-old potassic granite gneiss and is intruded by 2.5-Gyr-old undeformed potassic granite. The locations of samples J2212, J2302 and J2303 are shown. c, 3.95-Gyr-old banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212). The light-coloured layers, commonly less than 1 cm in width, are considered to be deformed granitic veins. d, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302). e, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303). Compared with sample J2212, there are fewer veins in J2302 and J2303 and these were removed during sample preparation. f, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302) shows a granoblastic texture and is composed of plagioclase, quartz and biotite, with minor microcline. g, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303) has a similar texture and mineral composition to J2302, except for containing less biotite. h, 3.95-Gyr-old banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212) consists of different components. The lower right contains more K-feldspar (monzogranitic layer) compared with the upper left (trondhjemitic layer), consistent with the banded characteristics in the field. Both layers show the same foliation defined by oriented biotite flakes.

a, 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302). b, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303). c, Banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212, including zircons analysed in two sessions from the same sample, marked as J2212A and J2212B). On the left are CL images and on the right are secondary electron images. MA and RC identify magmatic and recrystallized domains, respectively, whereas R represents overgrowth rims and grains newly formed during metamorphism. The analytical sites are marked with white circles, together with the analysis number and age. Secondary electron images show that the weakly modified zircons retain euhedral prismatic shapes, a typical characteristic of magmatic zircon. This feature is particularly evident in zircons from sample J2303, which have been less affected by metamorphism.

a, Zircon analyses of trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2302 define two concordant age groups at 3.95 Gyr and 3.45 Gyr, interpreted as the timing of magmatic crystallization and subsequent metamorphism, respectively. b, Most zircons in trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2303 are magmatic and cluster near 3.95 Gyr. Overgrowth rims show radiogenic Pb loss, including analysis 61.1R, which is the closest to concordia. c, Zircon analyses from banded trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2212 (including zircons analysed in two sessions from the same sample, marked as J2212A and J2212B) are more scattered, with the main population along a discordia line from 3.95 Gyr. However, several zircons with magmatic zoning yield concordant ages of 3.86–3.70 Gyr, potentially owing to the intrusion of thin granitic veins and/or partial resetting of the U–Pb system of 3.95-Gyr-old zircons. Analysis 63.1MA in J2212B has the oldest 207Pb/206Pb age of 3,989 ± 10 Myr but shows slightly reverse discordance, probably because of local enrichment of radiogenic Pb during later metamorphism98. d, Concordia diagram of all samples for analyses with <20% discordance. The weighted mean 207Pb/206Pb age of 3,951 ± 3 Myr (95% confidence level, MSWD = 1.15, n = 33) for magmatic/recrystallized cores is considered the best estimate for the magmatic crystallization age of the trondhjemitic gneiss protolith.

Zircon Lu–Hf isotope analyses were carried out in two sessions. Circles and triangles represent the results of the first analyses and squares represent the results of the second analytical session. All of the magmatic/recrystallized zircons with >3.9-Gyr 207Pb/206Pb age have homogeneous 176Hf/177Hf ratios except for J2302-2.1MA, which has a high 176Lu/177Hf ratio. The magmatic/recrystallized zircons with <3.9-Gyr 207Pb/206Pb age in samples J2302 and J2303 are all located near the Pb loss line. Some newly formed zircons have much higher 176Hf/177Hf ratios, which may be related to external fluids introduced during metamorphism.

a–c, REE patterns of zircons from the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (samples J2302, J2303 and J2212, respectively). The REE data were filtered using the methods suggested in ref. 26. d,e, Magmatic oxygen fugacity and H2O content of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss. The oxygen fugacity (fO2) was calculated using the oxybarometer proposed in ref. 82 based on the average REE content of the filtered magmatic zircons. The magmatic water content was calculated using the hygrometer established in ref. 26 and the effect of U loss in the whole rock was corrected assuming a Th/U ratio of 5 (ref. 26). Considering that the composition of sample J2212 may have been influenced by alteration and the intrusion of thin younger veins, the average composition of J2302 and J2303 was used for calculating the fO2 and water content of J2212.

a, An–Ab–Or diagram99. Note that sample J2212 plots in the granite field owing to the presence of thin younger granitic veins. The homogeneous 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (samples J2302 and J2303) is similar to the granitoids in Anshan and Nuvvuagittuq (mainly trondhjemitic gneiss) but different from those in Acasta, Tarim and Greenland (mainly tonalitic and granodioritic gneisses). b, Nb versus Ta diagram. c, Sr versus Y diagram. and d, La/Yb versus Yb classification diagrams for high-pressure, medium-pressure and low-pressure TTGs4. The 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss consistently plots in the high-pressure TTG field, being similar to the 3.72-Gyr-old Aktash gneiss in the Tarim Craton and some TTG rocks in Greenland but different from many other ≥3.8-Gyr-old granitoids around the world, which mostly plot into the medium-pressure and low-pressure TTG fields. Several samples from the literature that plot outside the ranges in b and d are not shown.

a,b, LILE contents of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss and potential source rocks (Supplementary Tables 6 and 7). The dashed red lines represent LILE contents required for the source to produce the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss by 7%, 10%, 20% and 30% melting, assuming that these elements are perfectly incompatible with bulk partition coefficient equal to 0. Considering that the degree of partial melting of a mafic rock source needs to be >7% for melt aggregation to form magma but <30% to match the high SiO2 contents of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss, the LILE contents of the source need to be in the grey shaded area. Because the sources of Eoarchaean TTGs are from mafic rocks, we have compiled the geochemical data of Eoarchaean mafic rocks worldwide (Methods and Supplementary Table 7). Comparing the LILE contents of these mafic rocks with those required to form the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss, the amphibolite group I in Acasta is the most suitable source to use for modelling, consistent with the fact that it is the only mafic rock >3.95 Gyr old. c, P–T pseudosection for the composition of amphibolite group I from Acasta, assuming X(H2O) = 1.5 wt% and Fe3+/(Fe3+ + Fe2+) ratio = 0.1. The dashed white lines represent the wt% of melt.

a–d, The red dot denotes the median sodic TTG composition4, which was assumed as the starting melt composition. Solid black and orange curves represent the effects of fractional crystallization of plagioclase and hornblende, respectively, whereas dashed black and orange curves represent the effects of accumulation of plagioclase and hornblende, respectively. Orange squares show the compositions of the 3.95-Gyr-old high-pressure TTGs from this study. Small dots represent melts produced by partial melting of the Acasta amphibolite group I (Supplementary Table 9), colour-coded by pressure. Comparison shows that plagioclase accumulation and hornblende fractional crystallization can explain the positive Eu and Sr anomalies in our samples (a,b) but they fail to simultaneously reproduce the high (La/Yb)N and (Gd/Yb)N ratios and the high SiO2 contents observed in the rocks (c,d). By contrast, melts formed under high-pressure conditions match well with the main geochemical characteristics of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic samples.

The positive εHf(t) values of magmatic zircons from the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss indicate that its basaltic precursor was young juvenile crust derived from a DMD. Even if the basaltic precursor (assuming 176Lu/177Hf = 0.022) was derived from a 4.5-Gyr-old DMD with a similar 176Lu/177Hf ratio (0.0384) to modern depleted mantle, its extraction time from the mantle could not be earlier than 4.0 Ga (solid blue line). If the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss was formed by partial melting of basalt immediately extracted from a DMD with similar 176Lu/177Hf ratio, then the timing of mantle depletion can be estimated to be about 4.35 Ga (dashed black line). Earlier depletion of the mantle is required if partial melting of a basaltic precursor occurred some time after its extraction from a DMD (dashed blue line) or the degree of depletion in the mantle is less than modern depleted mantle (dashed red line). If the basaltic precursor was derived from a possible ultra-depleted mantle proposed by some researchers100, the depletion can be slightly delayed. Nevertheless, the depletion still needs to be no later than 4.2 Ga even if the 176Lu/177Hf of the ultra-depleted mantle is as high as 0.041 (solid purple line). Therefore, a Hadean DMD is necessary to yield the Hf isotope composition of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss.

#1343. France star Desire Doue is left with gruesome tooth injury after PSG youngster suffered elbow smash to the face during Les Bleus' dismal defeat by Italy

Published: 06:41 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 13 November 2026

France star Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after being hit with a nasty elbow in France's 3-1 defeat to Italy in the Nations League.

The PSG winger was left in need of some emergency dental work by Italy's Davide Frattesi who caught the 21-year-old in the mouth while shielding the ball.

In his post match interview French boss Zinedine Zidane, when asked if Doue had lost a tooth, replied: 'Yeah I think so. We’re going to take him straight there, a tooth has come loose I think, we’ll take care of him starting tomorrow.'

It was a poor day all round for the Frenchman who not only had his tooth dislodged but was also unable to impact a poor game for Les Blues in which the Azzuri beat them at the San Siro.

To compound Doue's misery it was the offender Frattesi who scored Italy's second goal in the 3-1 win just six minutes before he performed some unorthodox dentistry.

The Lazio midfielder's goal completed the Italians' comeback after going 1-0 down to a Michael Olise goal just ten minutes in before Inter Milan's Francesco Esposito levelled things up just 16 minutes later.

Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after receiving an elbow in the mouth from Davide Fratessi

Fratessi got away with just a yellow card as Italy beat the French 3-1 at the San Siro

Frattesi gave Italy the lead early on in the second half before Esposito netted his second from the spot to put the game out of reach.

Speaking after the game Zidane was surprisingly positive about his team's performance despite the loss, saying that losing is, 'part of the process.'

The French then went onto say: 'The most important thing is creating chances. Hitting the post had an impact, but I'm not disappointed.

'I would have been if we hadn't created good possession. What we need to analyse is why we weren't at the right level off the ball.'

The World Cup winner was not entirely positive however, later saying: 'in the second half we ran into difficulties, especially defensively.'

The victory put Italy level on points with the French in Group A with both sides having won three drawn one and lost one.

But France will have an opportunity to right their wrongs and return to the top of the group on Sunday as they welcome Turkey.

But if Italy beat Belgium on the same day the French will have to settle for second.

#1342. Why England were unremarkable on Harry Kane's big night, the Ben White problem - and established star whose place could be under threat from Morgan Rogers, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 02:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:49 EST, 13 November 2026

England will head to Spain on Sunday for a Nations League shoot out with the World Champions. A win in Madrid could see Thomas Tuchel's team progress to the quarter-finals next March as group winners.

It wasn't always easy on Harry Kane's big night at Wembley against Croatia, though. Indeed this was probably England's worst performance since losing to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final last July.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the key issues emerging from last night's tight squeeze.

Self-defeating abuse of White is madness and must stop

In case nobody has noticed, England are not over stocked with competent right-backs.

Trent Alexander-Arnold isn't wholly trusted in big games by Thomas Tuchel, Reece James is always injured and Tino Livramento has also struggled to be available. Why, then, is a significant section of the England support so determined to drive Ben White away from the international scene?

White plays for Arsenal, the champions of England. He is a fine, versatile defender who would be gratefully received and appreciated by fans of most national teams in world football. He had issues with the previous England management regime and does not apologise for that.

Ben White was booed when he came on. The abuse towards the defender must stop

He spoke about it this week and made it clear he didn't wish to reopen old wounds. All that matters now is that he is willing and available. But – despite a plea from Tuchel before this game – England fans still booed him when he came on as a substitute last night.

It's a disgraceful way to treat a footballer who can be an asset to his country going forwards and it's something the England manager cares deeply about. Do we want to win the next Euros or not? Do we want our best players motivated and driven and part of the squad? Or do we want to faff about harbouring old grudges related to a situation in Qatar four winters ago that none of us really know that much about?

The choice is clear. If we are not careful, we will drive a good footballer away from the England set-up for good. It's madness.

Big night for Kane but questions for England

They came to celebrate Harry Kane and the England captain got his goal. Number 92 for the striker. Beneath all the fuss over England's talisman, however, this came perilously close to being a step backwards for Thomas Tuchel's England.

The England manager has been saying since the last international break in September and October that he wanted his team to go to Madrid on Sunday in with a shout at knocking Spain from the top of this Nations League Group. Had Croatia been a little smarter in front of goal at Wembley last night, England would have been heading for a dead rubber against the world champions.

Harry Kane scored on his big night as England edged out a 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley

It was a night to remember for Kane as he was honoured after receiving his record 126th cap

Three times in the last ten minutes of this game, Croatia had good opportunities to score a second goal and take a point from the game that would have been perfectly justified. So England crawled over the line but there was little here that was impressive with questions emerging once again about how capable really are when they don't have the ball.

Kane put it well himself afterwards when he said: 'You can't always expect things to be perfect. Of course, we know we can improve on a few bits and we will need to if we want to win on Sunday.'

Tuchel himself will perhaps have quiet concerns. One of the German's worries about this England team is that they sometimes struggle to take training performances on to the field and this was another case in point.

The ultimate target for this team is to win the home Euros in 2028 and the pressure will need handling in front of their own supporters if they are to do that. With that in mind, it's good to know that the FA are interested in hosting the finals of this Nations League competition next summer.

If England make it through next March's two-legged quarter-finals, they could do with some practice of playing high-stakes games at Wembley.

Asked last week on the day he announced his squad whether Jordan Pickford was still his number one goalkeeper, Tuchel was unequivocal.

'He is,' said Tuchel. 'But the competition is on there as well. Like for the outfield players. And James Trafford will get regular starts now, that's what we wanted. They shared the matches last time. There's an opportunity that we maybe do this again.'

Morgan Rogers impressed after opening the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour

Jordan Pickford starting against Croatia could lead to James Trafford playing against Spain

With all this in mind, it was expected that Trafford would start this game with Pickford getting the gloves for the one that really matters in Spain on Sunday. That wasn't the case, so we wait with interest to see what the England manager does in Madrid.

What nobody really wants is for a return to the situation we had in the 1980s when Ron Greenwood used to rotate between the late Ray Clemence and last night's guest of honour Peter Shilton.

England's back four is the one area of this team that can look unconvincing – they did again last night - and the last thing they need is not to know who their goalkeeper is from one match to the next. Tuchel is going to have to make a decision.

Interesting that Tuchel chose to put Dan Burn into his team for this game, despite the Newcastle defender not being in the original squad.

With Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa both absent with injuries, Everton's Jarrod Branthwaite would have expected to play on the left of Jarell Quansah here. Instead, Burn leapfrogged him in the queue and maybe we should have paid more attention to something Tuchel said the day before the game.

'Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,' said Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite clearly has a way to go before he's fully trusted to start by Thomas Tuchel

'You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a big voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe where they followed in a high press and to man-man. And of course he was with us at the World Cup so he is used a bit more to our style of play.'

That's all very well and logical but – that being the case – why was Branthwaite chosen ahead of Burn in the original group of 25 last Friday? Burn, as it happened, had a very good game last night.

Tuchel talks always about the value of players being in camp. 'The train is leaving the station,' is one of the England manager's more memorable quotes of recent times. Players like Cole Palmer, for example, have learned to their cost that missing meet-ups with injuries can be costly.

Bukayo Saka is not in that category and has plenty of credit in the bank with the England manager. However, Tuchel's fondness for Morgan Rogers is well known and Saka's absence does give him a way of getting the Chelsea player into his team. Rogers may be a number ten at heart but he was effective once again here out on the right side.

The 24-year-old was one of England's better players on a muted night against Croatia and he deserved his first half goal. He gives England a more direct, athletic dimension on the opposite flank to the more balletic offerings of Anthony Gordon. Food for thought for Tuchel at least as Saka continues his own battle against persistent injuries.

Bukayo Saka's long-term place in England's team could be under threat from Morgan Rogers

Newcastle United were pretty much an open door in the summer as they sold players left right and centre. Gordon to Barcelona to make sure the club was the right side of the financial guidelines and then Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal simply because the players made it known they wanted to go.

Strange, then, that Manchester United didn't make a proper move for left-back Lewis Hall. Admittedly this wasn't the most difficult match in which he will have ever played, but Hall was impressive once again.

With Luke Shaw so injury prone, Hall pretty much has the left-back berth sewn up for England but it feels as though he now needs to make the next step in his club career. United retain a nominal interest but who knows what incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino may think? It's hard to work out why United didn't try harder to sign him last summer. He has subsequently signed a new contract at Newcastle, of course.
